r8152: probe → rtl_check_vendor_ok uses usb_find_common_endpoints which requires in/out/intr endpoints to exist (it iterates over bNumEndpoints). Then alloc_all_mem reads alt->endpoint+2 for bInterval. usb_find_common_endpoints finds the interrupt endpoint wherever it is, but endpoint[2] assumes index 2. Is there any guarantee that the interrupt endpoint is at index 2? usb_find_common_endpoints iterates over all endpoints and finds int_in — no index guarantee. So a device where the interrupt endpoint is at index 0 or 1 (e.g., endpoints in order int, bulk out, bulk in) — check: usb_endpoint_num(intr) must == 3, i.e., endpoint number 3, and usb_endpoint_num(in)==1, out==2. But the index in the array is the order in which endpoint descriptors appear in the config blob, which is arbitrary. So a malicious device can order descriptors as [EP3 int in, EP2 bulk out, EP1 bulk in] — indices 0,1,2. Then endpoint[2] is the bulk-in EP1. bInterval read from a bulk descriptor. That's just a wrong interval value (OOB value used, not OOB access). Also, could bNumEndpoints == 3 always here? usb_find_common_endpoints requires in, out, and int endpoints, so at least 3 endpoints exist → endpoint[2] exists. So no OOB. content.thinking:
Now, `qmi_wwan_register_subdriver` is called from qmi_wwan_bind when a subdriver exists. Let me read qmi_wwan_bind lines 744-830 to see the context, and whether info->control has endpoints. The control interface in QMI/MBIM is a communication interface which normally has 1 interrupt endpoint. But a malicious device can provide 0 endpoints on the control interface — the union descriptor just says bMasterInterface0 = control interface number. /* map QMI/wwan function by a fixed interface number */
#define QMI_FIXED_INTF(vend, prod, num) \
	USB_DEVICE_INTERFACE_NUMBER(vend, prod, num), \
	.driver_info = (unsigned long)&qmi_wwan_info

/* devices requiring "set DTR" quirk */
#define QMI_QUIRK_SET_DTR(vend, prod, num) \
	USB_DEVICE_INTERFACE_NUMBER(vend, prod, num), \
	.driver_info = (unsigned long)&qmi_wwan_info_quirk_dtr

/* Gobi 1000 QMI/wwan interface number is 3 according to qcserial */
#define QMI_GOBI1K_DEVICE(vend, prod) \
	QMI_FIXED_INTF(vend, prod, 3)

#define QMI_GOBI_DEVICE(vend, prod) \
	QMI_FIXED_INTF(vend, prod, 0)
